Ephemeroptera, Diptera, and Plecoptera have the highest importance values (percent by weight times percent by number) in Howard Creek (Boyne and Ingram, 1975). Total biomass, and total density were found to be higher at upstream stations than at downstream stations (Figure 2-11A) as was species diversity. The faunal community in Howard Creek appeared to change along the stream.
Mean density and mean biomass in Howard Creek tributaries were lowest in Bad Creek and highest in Corbin Creek during 1974 (Figure 2-11B). Values for West Bad Creek are not included because of a paucity of data. Bad Creek values are also lower than the mean for all Howard Creek stations, although comparison of Figures 2-11A and 2-11B show that Bad Creek invertebrate density and biomass were greater han those at Howard Creek station H7. Mean density values ere influenced greatly by occasional large numbers of ipterans reported on isolated occasions at some stations.
Fish species known to exist in the Howard Creek Irainage include blacknose dace (Rhinichthys atratulus), bluehead chub (Nocomis leptocephalus), yellowfin shiner (Notropis lutipinnis), hornyhead chub (Nocomis biguttatus), striped jumprock (Moxostoma rupiscartes), mottled sculpin (Cottus bairdi), rainbow trout (Salmo gairdneri) brook trout (Salvelinus fontinalis), and brown trout (Salmo trutta) (Exhibits S and W, Bad Creek Application; Archer, 1968). Rainbow trout predominate among the fish that have been stocked periodically in Howard Creek. The State classified Howard Creek as a natural trout stream and current policy is to release fingerlings at major access points, although adult fish (200 mm or longer) were stocked from 1965 to 1970. Recent inventories of fish populations in the Howard Creek drainage conducted on three sample areas above and below Highway 171 are shown in Table 2-5. Highest densities of trout were in stream sections least affected by land use and road construction activities. An estimated 128 trout per acre (9.5 lbs/acre) were projected from the area sampled in 1973 in Upper Howard Creek while 125 trout per acre (7.4 lbs/acre) was the estimate for the Limberpole Creek sampling station. Lowest value was 29 trout (4.6 lbs/acre) for Howard Creek at the Old Whitewater Road Crossing below Highway 171. It is not known to what extent, if any, the release of fingerling trout on May 10, 1973, may have contributed to the total number of trout sampled from the Howard Creek drainage.
